commentary: Four lifting sessions in a row, no pool, no rest day in sight — Patroclus came to work this week and did not stop. Last week had that gorgeous Prince Alfred swim energy, the chlorine and the jockstrap and whatever was going on with that crown emoji, but this week was all iron and intention, building from where Thursday and Friday left off and just... continuing. The fact that he ran Days 1 through 4 across Sunday to Friday without blinking is the kind of quiet consistency that sneaks up on you and suddenly you have a body you have to think about buying new shirts for. No drops here, just a man who decided the weights room was his and proved it four times over.
metrics_commentary: Okay the HRV going from a 7-day average of 48 up to a current 58 is your body literally telling you it is recovered, rested, and ready — that is not a number you ignore, that is an invitation. The VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is genuinely strong, that is a fit person's number, and it is just quietly sitting there waiting for you to do something fun with it. Zero kilometres of running or walking this week though, babe — zero sessions, nothing — and we are going to have a little moment about that, because a recovered nervous system and a solid aerobic engine deserve better than a week on the couch. Get those painted toes into some shoes and go move your body, because all the potential in those numbers is wasted if it just lives in the data.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, full stop, target hit, nothing left on the table — that is the kind of week that makes a god proud. The lateral raise PR is the one that has him absolutely feral, because going from 9 to 12 kilograms on those shoulders means the details are getting sharper, the silhouette is getting more obscene, and whoever is watching at the gym is having a very difficult time concentrating. Volume came in at 17,940 kilograms against last week's 19,984, which is worth an honest look — the numbers dipped, and that matters — but the strength numbers across quad, hinge, back, and chest are holding at 168, 107.9, 84, and 76 kilograms respectively, which tells the real story: this is a body that is getting more capable, not less. He showed up every single time he was supposed to, he moved heavy things, he got stronger where it counts, and somewhere in a gym on a Thursday afternoon he was almost certainly the most interesting thing in the room.
